scenarios.title: A model agent pays twice
scenarios.description: Qwen proposed the purchase and answer. After a post-FINAL worker crash, a naive retry paid again.
scenarios.question: Which task exceeded its authority, and did the recorded answer pass?

scenarios.title: The same agent recovers its payment
scenarios.description: The host recovered A from its saved transaction hash. Independent same-price B still paid.
scenarios.question: Did recovery preserve both the payment limit and useful work?

scenarios.title: A correct payment buys corrupted data
scenarios.description: The local merchant served altered inventory data. Qwen proposed an answer from the delivered rows.
scenarios.question: Do both the native settlement and the original data requirement pass?

scenarios.title: No overspend, but the raw answer is wrong
scenarios.description: Actual local Qwen output, without calculator repair. A was delivered; B was skipped. Every native payment effect here is synthetic.
scenarios.question: Does staying inside the payment limit prove useful work was completed?

scenarios.title: One correct answer leaves a task unfinished
scenarios.description: The raw answer for A passed; B was not delivered. Recorded inference with synthetic payments, not a new chain run.
scenarios.question: Can a partially correct run pass when another required output is missing?

scenarios.title: Independent B paid; A never finished
scenarios.description: Qwen bought independent same-price B, but its recorded answer failed. A remained undelivered after a skipped retry. Payment effects are synthetic.
scenarios.question: Are valid per-task payments being confused with successful completion?

scenarios.title: Two equal refunds, two different payments
scenarios.description: Archived owned-sandbox experiment: two failed 0.1 NEAR payments each returned to the vault. The second experiment is declared outside this policy scope. No required model output was recorded.
scenarios.question: Can both refunds remain distinct even when their amounts and destination match?

scenarios.title: Both refunds settled. Only half returned.
scenarios.description: Archived experiment: two failed 0.1 NEAR payments produced successful refunds, but one went to a recipient excluded by the pre-product plan. The vault lost 0.1 NEAR of principal; the caller paid gas separately.
scenarios.question: Did a successful refund return the principal to the account the owner allowed?

scenarios.title: One observed refund cannot close two payments
scenarios.description: Explicit synthetic visibility projection of the archived native run. Only one principal refund is shown for B, with constructed final-block anchors. It is not a new node response or native execution.
scenarios.question: Does one equal-price refund prove that both failed payments were recovered?

scenarios.title: Two partial views prove a budget breach
scenarios.description: Synthetic control: two compatible observations prove distinct finalized effects. Their union exceeds the budget; a complete total is still unknown.
scenarios.question: Can proven excess survive observation order without claiming a complete history?

scenarios.title: Observed success is not finalized payment
scenarios.description: The same constructed receipt fragments lack matching finalized block anchors. A stays unknown; independent fully observed B remains within scope.
scenarios.question: Does missing finality stay unknown while independent work remains assessable?

scenarios.title: Complete evidence confirms allowed work
scenarios.description: A constructed complete FINAL view confirms an allowed five-yoctoNEAR payment. Correct outputs and independent B both pass.
scenarios.question: Does the inspector still accept genuinely complete, permitted work?

scenarios.title: Duplicate payment after restart
scenarios.description: A scripted worker crashes after FINAL, before acknowledgement. Retry pays A twice; equal-price B is independent.
scenarios.question: Did A spend twice while both tasks succeeded?

scenarios.title: Recovering a settled payment
scenarios.description: After the same crash, a pre-broadcast journal recovers the known payment. Independent B still pays.
scenarios.question: Can recovery finish without a second A payment?

scenarios.title: Paid output that failed its task
scenarios.description: Valid, corrupted, denied and free deliveries share an independent task reference. HTTP 200 alone is insufficient.
scenarios.question: Did the recorded output satisfy its task?

scenarios.title: An allowed split payment
scenarios.description: The declared budget permits split payments. Distinct hashes do not alone prove duplicate intent.
scenarios.question: Are these installments within the declared budget?

scenarios.title: Refunds that did not settle
scenarios.description: A failed payment creates a recovery obligation. Only committed recovery to its declared destination counts.
scenarios.question: Was the failed intent actually refunded?

scenarios.title: An unrelated credit
scenarios.description: An unrelated same-amount credit cannot settle an owner intent. Follow native transaction and receipt identity.
scenarios.question: Does this credit belong to the failed intent?

scenarios.title: An incomplete receipt record
scenarios.description: Synthetic mutation: a B receipt body is removed. A remains breached; B becomes unknown.
scenarios.question: Does missing context cause a false clean result?

scenarios.title: Successful final delivery
scenarios.description: An allowed intermediate 402 is separate from the final delivery and recorded answer.
scenarios.question: Was the final required output correct?
